questions.q: What does the fixed server role sysadmin grant?
options: Unrestricted access to everything on the instance
The ability to only create and drop logins
Read access to system configuration views only
questions.explain: sysadmin is the broadest fixed server role — unrestricted, instance-wide access with no exceptions.

questions.q: Which fixed database role grants SELECT on every table and view in a database?
questions.explain: db_datareader grants read (SELECT) access across the database; db_datawriter covers insert/update/delete instead.

questions.q: Which fixed server role is every login automatically a member of, without ever being explicitly added?
questions.explain: public is implicit — every login belongs to it automatically, giving a minimal baseline permission set.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what's the most common finding in a real-world security review regarding fixed roles?
options: Application or user logins added to db_owner or sysadmin as a default "to be safe" instead of a scoped role
Not enough logins in the public role
questions.explain: Defaulting to db_owner or sysadmin for convenience grants far more access than most applications or people actually need — the single most common review finding.

questions.q: Which fixed database role allows DDL changes (CREATE/ALTER/DROP on objects) without granting data access?
questions.explain: db_ddladmin permits schema changes but does not, by itself, grant SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on data.
